overview: Seventeenth-century French projects joined engineering, landscape design and royal display. This chapter pairs a working waterway with Versailles to show different purposes of large-scale construction.

items.text: The Canal du Midi project used locks, aqueducts, bridges, spillways and tunnels to make an inland water route. UNESCO dates the wider historic works to 1667 through 1694.
The canal's water-supply system drew on the Montagne Noire. The Saint-Ferreol dam was a major engineering component.
After 1661, Louis XIV enlarged Versailles through work directed first by Le Vau and later by Jules Hardouin-Mansart. Its architecture developed across successive campaigns.
Andre Le Notre organized Versailles' gardens with long axes, planted beds, hedges, water and fountains. The landscape formed part of the royal residence's design.

sources.title: UNESCO, Palace and Park of Versailles
